metadata.source: Gyaltsen Namdrol: Pratityasamutpadahrdaya and Aryadharmadhatugarbhavivarana. Sarnath : CIHTS 1997, p. 29

children.translated_text: The twelve distinct members, taught by the Sage (<s>Muni</s>) as dependently arisen,
are properly subsumed within three (categories): afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), actions (<s>karma</s>), and suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). (Verse 1)

children.text: ādyāṣṭamanavamāḥ syuḥ kleśāḥ karma dvitīyadaśamau ca /
children.translated_text: The first, eighth, and ninth are afflictions; the second and tenth are action;

children.text: śeṣāḥ sapta ca duḥkhaṃ trisaṅgrahā dvādaśa tu dharmāḥ // Pshk_2 //
children.translated_text: and the remaining seven are suffering. Thus, these twelve <s>dharmas</s> are subsumed in three groups. (Verse 2)

children.text: tribhyo bhavati dvandvaṃ dvandvātprabhavanti sapta saptabhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the three (afflictions) arises the pair (of actions); from the pair arise the seven (sufferings); from the seven,

children.text: traya udbhavanti bhūyastadeva[tu] bhramati bhavacakram // Pshk_3 //
children.translated_text: the three arise again — thus revolves the wheel of existence (<s>bhavacakra</s>). (Verse 3)
The entire world is (nothing but) cause and effect; there is no other being here whatsoever.

children.text: śūnyebhya eva śūnyā dharmāḥ prabhavanti dharmebhyaḥ // Pshk_4 //

children.translated_text: By means of (the analogies of) recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>), lamp, seal, mirror, sound, sun-crystal (<s>arkakānta</s>), seed, and sour taste,
the continuity of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) and the non-transmigration (of any entity) should be ascertained by the wise. (Verse 5)
One who imagines annihilation (<s>uccheda</s>) even in the subtlest thing —
that ignorant person does not see the meaning of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). (Verse 6)
Nothing whatsoever is to be removed from this, nor is anything to be added.

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ bhūtadarśī vimucyate // Pshk_7 //
children.translated_text: Reality is to be seen as it truly is — one who sees reality is liberated. (Verse 7)

body.translated_text: The <s>Pratītyasamutpādahṛdayakārikā</s> (Heart Verses on Dependent Origination), composed by the teacher <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, is completed.
